$comment: Version literals that are repeated outside the mise configuration, and the one site that owns each of them.
scripts/pin_integrity.mjs re-extracts every entry here and fails when a copy disagrees with its authority, or when a copy has moved and is therefore no longer being compared at all.
mise-declared tools do not belong here: the same script derives those automatically from every mise.toml, its adjacent lockfile, and the other mise configs.

managerCoverage.description: Every mise configuration in the tree must be reachable by Renovate's native mise manager. The build and job images use non-standard basenames that the manager's defaults do not match, so renovate.json overrides its managerFilePatterns; an override replaces the defaults outright, and a new docker/<name>-mise.toml would otherwise be silently unmanaged.

pins.name: mise
pins.description: The mise binary is curl-bootstrapped in both images. It is the one tool no lockfile can pin, so the two Dockerfiles are the only record of it and must agree.

pins.name: sccache
pins.description: The job image asserts the installed sccache version in its build. The assertion is a second copy of the pin and goes stale silently unless it is compared.

pins.name: mr-boxington
pins.description: Same shape as sccache: the job image greps mbx --version for a literal that repeats the mise pin.

pins.name: rust
pins.description: rust-toolchain.toml is the single source of truth for the compiler. Every mise lockfile mirrors the resolved version, and mise exports RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN from the lock entry, so a stale lock keeps building with the old compiler however the declaration reads.
